title: A Hollow for the Spire
premise: Marguerite Montrose survives in the walled city of Vell by stealing memories and selling them as charms, hiding his own stolen past behind a false name. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, magic floods back into a country that has spent a generation pretending it never existed — and Marguerite discovers his memories were taken from him, not by him. Hunted by the Spire's remnant inquisitors and bound to a disgraced ward-keeper named Ilse who remembers his true face, he must cross a darkening country to reach the Hollow Door, the last way out of a nation being erased by winter. In the end, Marguerite chooses to give back every memory he ever stole — including his own name — to reopen the Door for others, remaining inside a country that no longer exists but is no longer empty.
about_author: O. M. Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three thousand unlabeled letters before turning to fiction. They live somewhere cold, write only at night, and refuse to confirm which city they were born in.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A night of petty thefts in Vell: he lifts a widow's memory of her wedding and sells it back to her as a luck-charm. The beat establishes his charm, his guilt, and the rule that keeps him alive — never steal anything you can't sell twice.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The sky goes black mid-market; the border wards fall with a sound like a bell breaking. Panic spreads, and Marguerite feels something unlock inside his own head — a sealed room he didn't know he had. Beat: dread mixed with a terrible sense of recognition.

chapters.title: Ilse at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A disgraced ward-keeper drags a half-dead stranger off the collapsed gatehouse — and freezes, because she recognizes his face from files she was ordered to burn. She lies to her superiors to keep him alive. Beat: duty cracking under an old debt.

chapters.title: What the Seals Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Under Ilse's questioning, the seal on his mind frays: fragments surface of a tower, a white coat, a child's hand. He realizes his five years of thieving were someone else's design. Beat: vertigo of discovering your life is a forgery.

chapters.title: The Remnant
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Corvane's POV. The Spire's surviving inquisitors regroup in the flooded undercity, hunting 'unregistered vessels' — people whose minds hold sealed magic. Marguerite's description lands on Corvane's desk. Beat: cold institutional menace beginning to move.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Candlelight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ilse offers Marguerite a deal: she knows the road to the Hollow Door; he carries something in his head that can open it. Neither trusts the other. Beat: two survivors negotiating intimacy as a transaction.

chapters.title: Leaving Vell
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They slip out during a curfew riot, past wards that now hum with returning wild magic. Marguerite steals one last charm — Ilse's memory of her court-martial — and immediately regrets it. Beat: guilt sharpening into self-knowledge.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The north road unspools wrong: villages missing from maps, signposts pointing at nothing. Winter falls unnaturally fast behind them. Beat: the country itself becoming hostile, erasure made landscape.

chapters.title: The Memory Market at Ashford
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A refugee town where stolen memories are the only currency left. Marguerite finds a seller offering a memory of the Spire's inner tower — his tower. Buying it nearly gets them both caught. Beat: temptation versus survival.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The inquisitor interrogates a captured thief gently, almost lovingly, extracting the pair's route. We learn Corvane helped seal Marguerite's mind years ago — and believes he is saving him. Beat: antagonist as sincere believer.

chapters.title: What Ilse Burned
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Around a fire, Ilse confesses she was ordered to destroy records of the Spire's memory experiments and obeyed — except one file, the one with Marguerite's face. Her debt is why she's here. Beat: love beginning to take the shape of atonement.

chapters.title: The Tower in the Snow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They shelter in an abandoned watchtower that Marguerite inexplicably knows room by room. His sealed memories break open further: he was a Spire artificer who built the memory-seals himself. Beat: horror at complicity in his own erasure.

chapters.title: Hollow Country
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They cross a valley where an entire town's population stands frozen mid-task, their memories harvested wholesale. Ilse wants to help them; Marguerite says it's impossible. First real fight between them. Beat: love against duty, openly declared.

chapters.title: The Thief's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He takes stock of every memory he's stolen in five years and realizes each one was a component — pieces of a key scattered across buyers' heads. The Door needs them all returned. Beat: purpose crystallizing from shame.

chapters.title: Ambush on the Causeway
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Corvane's remnant corners them on a flooded causeway. Ilse holds the line alone so Marguerite can run, and is captured. Beat: sacrifice that transforms their bargain into something neither will name yet.

chapters.title: Alone With the Key
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He could reach the Door without her. Instead he turns back toward Corvane's camp, finally understanding that the last piece of the key isn't in a buyer's head — it's the memory of who he was. Beat: choosing love over escape.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane offers Marguerite restoration: full memory, full power, a place in the rebuilt Spire — if he surrenders the key. Marguerite sees the trap and, briefly, the lonely man inside it. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In a cell, Marguerite deliberately shatters his own seal, flooding back every memory at once — the experiments, the children, his name. He frees Ilse amid the backlash. Beat: identity reclaimed at maximum cost.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They flee north through total dark as the country begins literally forgetting itself — roads dissolving, names unwriting. Only the Hollow Door remains fixed. Beat: desperate, beautiful final flight together.

chapters.title: The Hollow Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the Door, the key requires return of everything he stole — including his own name and history, given up willingly. He pours himself into the lock. Beat: climax as renunciation; the door opens not outward but for everyone still inside.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The Door opens onto the frozen towns waking, memories streaming home. Ilse searches the crowd for the man she knew and finds instead someone new wearing his face — nameless, lighter, staying. Beat: grief and grace entwined.

chapters.title: What He Sold Twice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue. Spring comes late to a country rebuilding its memory. A nameless man sells small charms again — but now he gives them away, and keeps one for himself: a wedding he never attended, belonging to a widow in Vell. Beat: quiet resolution; identity chosen, not recovered.
